title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee, was arrested at gunpoint by US marshals in July 2025 and falsely charged with bank theft in Fargo, North Dakota. She was held for about six months, first in Tennessee for almost four months without bail and then in North Dakota for about two more months. The charges were dropped on Christmas Eve after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee when the fraud happened. She is suing for $10m.

The federal lawsuit names Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck. Lipps says police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and did not properly investigate before seeking her arrest. She claims the city lacked policy, training, and supervision for facial recognition use. Fargo said it does not discuss active lawsuits. The lawsuit is ongoing.
